notes: null. webfetch returns HTTP 403 for every path on this host, including image files, so I opened the stored official_source_url and the site homepage in Playwright (the brief's section 2 step 4) and enumerated every , every computed background-image and every icon link. The stored programme page (in.emb-japan.go.jp/education/japanese_government_scholarships.html) carries exactly two images - testimages/jp_flag.gif (the national flag) and testimages/index_images8.jpg (alt 'Random Image', a decorative banner) plus a title_bg.jpg background. No logo anywhere. The homepage has no logo either: its only institutional-looking asset, files/000061767.png, is not a mark at all - I pixel-analysed it (419x200, 92.7% transparent, 100% of its opaque pixels pure white) and rendered it on the header blue, where it appears as a decorative white dot-matrix world map. Every other image is programme artwork for unrelated initiatives (Japan Month, Visit Japan Web, Click! Japan Photo Contest, Skill Development Support / JICA, ALPS treated water, Blue Sky Initiatives), i.e. rule 1 (banners) and rule 2 (other bodies) both exclude them. The parent-domain fallback that rule 1 allows does not exist: both www.emb-japan.go.jp and emb-japan.go.jp fail with net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED. Finally, the awarding body for this record is MEXT (the embassy only recommends candidates under the Embassy Recommendation route), and MEXT's mark is published only on mext.go.jp, which is a sibling ministry domain rather than the shard host, a subdomain of it, or a parent of it - so rule 1 puts it out of scope, and the embassy/MOFA mark that is in scope would be the wrong body under rule 2. Honest null per rule 7: nothing acceptable exists, and an MOFA emblem on a MEXT scholarship would be exactly the provenance error rule 2 warns about.
